title: Finite direct diagrams in a Brown localization
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functor categories and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with initial object $0$ and classes $C,W$ of arrows containing isomorphisms and closed under composition. Suppose $W$ has two-out-of-three and is retract closed, every $0\to X$ belongs to $C$, every arrow factors as a member of $C$ followed by a member of $W$, pushouts of members of $C$ along arbitrary arrows exist and belong to $C$, and pushouts of members of $C\cap W$ belong to $C\cap W$. Let $q:N(\mathcal A)\to L$ be its homotopy coherent localization, universal on entire coherent functor categories for inverting $W$. Let $I$ be an ordinary category with finitely many objects and morphisms and a degree function to $\mathbf N$ such that every nonidentity arrow strictly raises degree. Let $W_I$ be the natural transformations of strict functors $I\to\mathcal A$ whose components belong to $W$. Evaluation and $q$ induce an equivalence
$$N(\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal A))[W_I^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),L).$$
Moreover every coherent diagram $N(I)\to L$ is coherently naturally equivalent to $q\circ N(D)$ for some strict $D:I\to\mathcal A$. In particular every object of $L$ is equivalent to some $qX$. The empty category, the singleton and the span category $(0\leftarrow1\to2)$ are allowed. No arbitrary coproducts, functorial factorization, fibrations or model structure are assumed.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.6.17, printed pp. 394-395 (PDF pp. 409-410), and the localization construction of section 7.1 (essential surjectivity on objects); ordinary all-cofibrant case of Definition 7.4.12.
